commonPoints: Gun safe weight ranges from a few pounds (handgun boxes) to well over 1,000 lb
Size, steel gauge and fire insulation drive weight
Heavier usually means harder to steal, but weight alone is not security
Check the floor before placing a heavy safe upstairs
Do not move a heavy safe alone; professional delivery is common
Guns and contents add weight on top of the empty figure

ourGain.point: Same capacity, very different weight: Liberty Centurion 24 (375 lb) vs AMSEC BFII6636 (24 long guns, 1,716 lb), so gun count alone predicts little
Footprint math: empty weight divided by footprint in square feet, set against the IRC design live load (40 psf, 30 psf in sleeping rooms) as context for an engineer, not a pass/fail test

Who certified the fire rating differs by weight class: AMSEC states an ETL 120-minute rating at 1200F on the 1,716 lb BFII6636, while Liberty's Centurion 30-40 minute ratings are stated by Liberty without a named lab
Weight comes with a minimum doorway: Liberty lists 18 in for the Centurion 12 and 25.75 in for the Centurion 32
Plan on loaded weight, not empty weight, as owners on FirearmsTalk and The High Road advise

painPoints.pain: Worry that the floor or stairs cannot take the weight of a loaded safe
painPoints.details: Owners wanting the safe upstairs or in a basement room ask about floor load ratings, bracing basement stairs and the combined weight of safe plus contents.

quotes.text: Most residential floors are only rated for about 40 lb per sq ft.
Consider what the full of stuff weight will be, and plan accordingly.

painPoints.pain: Unsure whether an upstairs apartment floor can hold a loaded 400-700 lb gun safe
painPoints.details: Second-floor renters ask how heavy a safe they can get away with. Replies say it is usually fine near a load-bearing wall or on plywood, and to add the weight of the guns and ammo.

quotes.text: weigh each of your firearms, accessories, and ammo that will be going in there, and add it to the weight of your safe.

painPoints.pain: A 500 lb+ safe cannot be carried up stairs by the owner without risk of injury or damage
painPoints.details: Owners are told to hire safe movers, check the stairs and use door removal or modular safes.

painPoints.pain: Safe will not make the turn or doorway, and the dolly is rated below the safe weight
painPoints.details: Owners hit tight stair turns, narrow doors and dollies rated to 600 or 800 lb.

painPoints.pain: Small light safes can be carried off, and owners are unsure how or whether to bolt them
painPoints.details: Buyers of lighter safes debate bolting for theft versus tip-over.
